title: Step-by-Step Guide to Excel Reporting in Business Central
summary: Excel reporting in Business Central allows developers to create data-driven reports that users can easily customize with pivot tables and charts. The post demonstrates building a customer activity report and uploading the customized layout back to Business Central so updates appear automatically in future runs.
key_points: Excel reports use a dataset with nested dataitems and dataitemlink to structure data hierarchically
RequestFilterFields at the dataitem level prompt users for filter parameters at runtime
Excel layouts can be customized with pivot tables and charts, then uploaded back to Business Central as the default layout
Business Central updates the data tabs while preserving custom tabs created by users

quotes.text: Microsoft Excel Reports are the easiest for end users to modify, and one of the easiest data sets to create.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains why Excel is a good choice for accessible, user-friendly reporting in Business Central
